style.vernacular: Small windswept British-style harbour town on a north-facing slope: one- and two-storey houses built of wood and iron (timber frames clad in painted render or corrugated iron, a few stone and brick civic buildings), with brightly painted corrugated-metal roofs in red, green and blue, carved wooden fascia boards, porches and well-kept gardens. Treeless peat moorland behind, cypress hedges and gorse in gardens, red British post and telephone boxes.
style.ornament: Carved wooden fascia boards and bargeboards, porches, bay windows, white-painted window frames, gardens with hedges and fuchsia, whalebone arch and red phone boxes as town icons. Wall and roof colours are typical of Stanley's bright painted houses as described in sources, not measured hex values.

sources.what: Falkland houses known for bright paint, carved wooden fascia boards, timber kit houses; Britannica 1911 called Stanley's houses wood and iron
north-facing slope, subpolar oceanic climate, Government House 1845, peat stacks, red post and telephone boxes
grey stone Government House with slate roof, conservatory with grapevine
